metaDescription: Five 24 inch compact front-load washers compared on drum size, spin speed, steam, stackability and hookups, for apartments, closets, RVs and tiny homes.
expertTake: The LG 24 inch 2.4 cu ft stackable washer is the best overall pick because it adds an AI fabric sensor and steam to a proven compact platform. The CONTOURE 2.7 cu ft is the value pick, with the biggest drum and a 1400 RPM spin in the group. Anyone who needs drying in the same machine should look at a washer-dryer combo instead of a washer-only unit. Prices move, so treat tiers as relative.
introParagraphs: A 24 inch compact washer is a front-loading machine sized for the places a full washer will not go: apartments, closets, tiny homes, boats and RVs with a proper laundry nook. It plugs into a normal outlet, needs a cold water supply and drains into a standpipe or sink.

Compact does not mean simple. Drum size, spin speed, vibration and what the machine needs from your plumbing all differ, and those differences decide whether a washer is a pleasure or a daily annoyance.

products.name: LG 24 in 2.4 cu ft stackable front-load washer with steam
products.description:
LG's compact washer packs a 2.4 cubic foot drum into a 24 inch wide cabinet and adds an AI fabric sensor that detects fabric type and load size to adjust the cycle. Steam cleaning targets stains and allergens, and the unit pairs with a matching compact dryer for stacking. LG is the most widely supported brand in the 24 inch class, which helps with parts and service.

The 2.4 cu ft drum is a little smaller than the 2.7 cu ft models here, so you give up a few pounds per load. It sits in the upper-middle price tier, above the Kenmore and CONTOURE. Compared with the BLACK+DECKER, you pay for the sensor, the steam and the brand support. Compared with the Equator, it offers far more drum.

Ownership is routine for a front loader. Leave the door ajar after a wash, wipe the door boot, use HE detergent and level the four feet so it does not walk. Remove the transit bolts before the first load and keep the manual for the drain height spec.
products.bestFor: Apartments and tiny homes that value brand support and smart cycles.
cons: Smaller 2.4 cu ft drum than 2.7 models

products.name: CONTOURE 24 in 2.7 cu ft stackable washer, 1400 RPM
products.description:
CONTOURE offers a 2.7 cubic foot drum, 1400 RPM spin, 16 wash cycles and five temperature settings in a 24 inch stackable cabinet. The drum is the largest in the group and the spin matches the fastest. A higher spin pulls more water from the clothes, which shortens drying time if you use a separate dryer.

The tradeoff is brand reach. It is a lesser-known name than LG or Kenmore, so parts and service take more effort to source. It sits in the lower-middle tier, which is the argument for it. Compared with the BLACK+DECKER, it has a faster spin; compared with the LG, it lacks the AI sensor.

Ownership is routine. Level it carefully, because 1400 RPM spin transmits vibration to a weak floor, and use HE detergent in measured amounts. Large drums also cut the number of loads per week.
products.bestFor: Small families that want the biggest drum for the money.
cons: Fast spin needs a stiff floor

products.name: Kenmore 2.2 cu ft compact front-load washer, steam relax
products.description:
Kenmore's compact front loader has a 2.2 cubic foot drum, 15 wash cycles including workout wear, wool and delicates, and a steam option that relaxes wrinkles at the end of the cycle. Express Wash and Accela Wash shorten cycles for small loads. It is a familiar American brand with broad retail and service reach.

The drum is the smallest of the washer-only models, so large bedding will not fit. It sits in the lower-middle tier. Compared with the CONTOURE, it has a smaller drum but a more established name; compared with the LG, it lacks the AI sensor but includes the wrinkle steam.

Ownership is routine. Run a tub clean cycle monthly, wipe the boot and keep the door ajar after use. Ask whether delivery includes the stacking kit if needed. Large comforters do not fit, so plan for the laundromat now and then.
products.bestFor: Singles and couples who want a known brand and quick cycles.
pros: 15 cycles with workout wear and wool

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 2.7 cu ft front-load washer, 16 cycles
products.description:
BLACK+DECKER sells a 2.7 cubic foot front loader with a stainless steel tub, 16 cycles, an LED display, automatic unbalance detection and a 1300 RPM spin. At about 23.4 inches wide, it fits tight spaces, and the unbalance detection helps keep the spin from shaking the room.

The features are basic by design. There is no steam or smart sensing, and spin is a little slower than the CONTOURE. It sits in the lowest tier of the group, which is the argument for it. Compared with the Kenmore, it has more drum but fewer premium touches.

Ownership is routine: level, leave the door ajar and use HE detergent. The stainless tub resists staining.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want 2.7 cu ft without extras.

products.name: Equator 24 in ultra compact washer 1.57 cu ft with vented dryer
products.description:
Equator pairs a 1.57 cubic foot washer with a 2.6 cubic foot vented dryer as two independent, stackable 24 inch units. Two machines mean you can wash one load while drying another, which no combo can do. The washer adds a pet cycle meant to lift hair, odors and dander.

The washer drum is the smallest in the guide, and a vented dryer needs an exhaust duct to the outdoors, which many apartments and RVs cannot provide. It sits in the top price tier of the group. Compared with the LG, it gives you a matching dryer in the box but a much smaller drum.

Ownership requires cleaning the dryer lint trap each load and the duct yearly. Plan the venting before you buy. Both units are independent, so a failure in one does not stop the other.
products.bestFor: Homes with a vent path that want a stacked wash-and-dry set.

products.name: Midea 24 in 2.7 cu ft ventless washer-dryer combo, 1400 RPM
products.description:
Midea's combo is the one machine here that also dries, using a ventless system so no duct is needed. It offers a 2.7 cubic foot drum, 1400 RPM spin, steam care and an overnight wash-and-dry cycle that lets you load it at bedtime and wake to dry clothes. For a closet, a boat or an RV with no way to vent, that convenience is the entire point.

The tradeoff is time and capacity. Ventless condensing drying is slow, and the dry load is smaller than the wash load, so a full drum of towels will come out damp. It sits in the middle of the price range. Compared with the washer-only models, it saves a second machine but costs hours per load; compared with the Equator set, it needs no duct but cannot wash and dry two loads at once.

Ownership requires cleaning the lint filter each dry cycle and descaling the condenser path occasionally. Leave the door ajar between uses and give it a cold water supply for the condenser.
products.bestFor: Ventless closets and RVs that want one machine for both jobs.
pros: Washes and dries in one drum
cons: Dry load smaller than wash load
Needs cold water for the condenser

buyingCriteria.explanation: The CONTOURE and BLACK+DECKER offer 2.7 cu ft, the LG 2.4, the Kenmore 2.2 and the Equator 1.57. A 2.7 cu ft drum washes roughly a queen comforter with care, while 1.57 handles a few days of clothes. Match the drum to the household. A rule of thumb is to wash only as much as fills the drum loosely, about three quarters full. Overloading is the top cause of poor cleaning and imbalance errors in compact machines. Weigh a typical load before you shop, because most people overestimate.

The CONTOURE spins at 1400 RPM and the BLACK+DECKER at 1300. Faster spin extracts more water and shortens drying, but it also shakes the floor. A stiff floor and careful leveling matter. Anti-vibration pads under the feet help on a wood floor. A 1400 RPM spin on a 150 pound machine is a lot of energy for a flexible floor to absorb.

Most 24 inch washers need a cold water tap and a standpipe or sink drain, typically 30 to 36 inches high. Check the manual for drain height. An RV laundry nook may need a pump. A small drain pump kit helps when no standpipe is nearby. RV owners should also check gray tank capacity, since a wash uses 10 to 20 gallons.

The LG, CONTOURE and Equator list stacking. A stacked pair saves floor space but needs a stacking kit and a dryer. Measure ceiling height and door swing. Stacking kits are often sold separately. Ceiling height with a stacked pair often runs around 6 feet, so check clearance. Door swing matters too, since a front door that opens into a wall is useless.

The LG has an AI sensor and steam, the Kenmore a wrinkle-relax steam option and the Equator a pet cycle. Features cost money and add parts. Pick the ones you will use. Steam helps but does not replace detergent. Quick cycles under 30 minutes are the feature most small households use daily.

LG and Kenmore have wide service networks, while CONTOURE and Equator are smaller. A broken compact washer is hard to ship. Weigh support against the price tier. Ask about parts before buying. Registering the warranty on day one is cheap insurance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared drum sizes from 1.57 to 2.7 cu ft. Drum size is the one spec you cannot change later. We also noted that real usable capacity is about three quarters of the label.

howWeEvaluated.title: Spin and vibration
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted 1300 and 1400 RPM and unbalance detection. Vibration matters in apartments. A fast spin helps only if the floor can take it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Features
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited sensors, steam and quick washes. Features should be used, not just listed. We gave no credit for features that need an app and a Wi-Fi password in a closet.

howWeEvaluated.title: Support
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed LG and Kenmore reach against smaller brands. Service access is a cost. Service access also affects resale.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: We judged tiers from BLACK+DECKER to Equator. The Midea combo changes the value math by saving a whole second machine.

howToChoose.intro: Household size decides drum size, and drum size decides how many loads you wash each week. A single person and a family of four sit at opposite ends of this guide.
Tiers are relative and move often. In this class the extra spend mostly buys smart cycles, support and an included dryer. The lowest tier here is the BLACK+DECKER.

howToChoose.subheading: Washer Only vs Wash and Dry Set

cards.label: Washer only
cards.text: LG, CONTOURE, Kenmore and BLACK+DECKER need a separate dryer or a line.

cards.label: Set
cards.text: Equator includes a vented dryer but needs ducting.

howToChoose.note: If you cannot vent, plan to line dry or buy a ventless dryer. A ventless combo is the way out if you cannot duct, but it is slow.

howToChoose.subheading: For RV and Tiny Home Use Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: 120V power, a small water footprint, and a drain you can reach.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Kenmore and LG fit small nooks, the CONTOURE lists RV use. The Midea combo adds a drying option without ducting.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want smart cycles and brand support, pointing to the LG. That also buys longer service reach.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You just need a drum, pointing to the BLACK+DECKER. Choose a basic drum and a line for drying.

maintenance.why: Prevents mildew smell. Use a manufacturer tub cleaner or a hot cycle with an approved cleaner.
Trapped water breeds mold. Dry the folds of the boot. Look for black spots, which signal mold.
Leaks begin at clamps. Replace brittle hoses before they burst.
Unlevel machines walk and bang. Tighten the lock nuts after leveling.
Clogged filters slow draining. Place a towel under the filter door to catch water.

faq.a: Yes. A standpipe or sink drain at the right height. A drain pump kit can help when none is nearby. A standpipe at about 30 to 36 inches is typical. Check the maximum drain height before you pick a spot.
HE detergent in measured amounts. Too much soap leaves residue and causes odors.
Tiers run from BLACK+DECKER to the Equator set. Prices change, so check listings. Spending more buys features and support, not a bigger drum.

faq.q: Can I use it in an RV?
faq.a: If you have 120V, fresh water and a drain. Check the gray tank capacity too. Also check the weight, since these machines run 150 pounds or more.
Trapped moisture. Leave the door ajar. A monthly tub clean prevents it. Detergent residue is the other common cause.

faq.q: Do I need to remove transit bolts?
faq.a: Yes, before first use. Skipping them damages the machine on the first spin.
